_notice: DEMO DATA. Illustrative university support knowledge base written for the hackathon. It is NOT official University of Debrecen information and contains no real contact details.

entries.scope: Campus Wi-Fi (eduroam) and wired network problems.
procedures: Forget the eduroam network on the device and reconnect using the full university username and password.
Check whether the problem affects other devices or other students in the same room to tell a device issue from a network outage.
As a temporary workaround use a wired connection, a computer lab, or a mobile hotspot.
Report the outage to the IT Service Desk with building, room, time it started, device type and the error message.
entries.contact_channel: IT Service Desk ticket form or help desk counter (see the official university IT page)
entries.typical_response: Same working day for building-wide outages

entries.scope: University accounts, student portal (Neptun), e-learning platform access.
procedures: Use the official password reset page for the university account.
Try a private browser window and clear cookies to rule out a cached session problem.
If the account is locked or multi-factor authentication fails, contact the IT Service Desk with the student ID (never share the password).
entries.contact_channel: IT Service Desk ticket form (see the official university IT page)

entries.scope: Damaged furniture, building fabric, heating, lighting, cleaning.
procedures: Stop using the damaged item and move it aside or mark it so nobody else uses it.
Note the building, room number and a short description; take a photo if possible.
Report the damage to Facilities Management (building reception / porter's desk or the facilities request form).
If the room becomes unusable for a scheduled class, inform the instructor so the class can be moved.
entries.contact_channel: Building reception / porter's desk or facilities request form
entries.typical_response: Usually within a few working days for non-urgent repairs

entries.scope: Classroom audio-visual and teaching equipment.
procedures: Check cables and the input source selection before reporting.
Report the faulty equipment with room number to the building reception, which forwards it to the technical team.
Ask the instructor to request a room change if the class cannot run without the equipment.
entries.contact_channel: Building reception / porter's desk
entries.typical_response: Same day for teaching-critical equipment when reported early

entries.scope: Exams, deadlines, retakes, academic exceptions.
procedures: If a technical or other problem may affect an exam, inform the examiner or course instructor BEFORE the exam starts if at all possible.
Document the problem (time, screenshots, error messages, witnesses) as evidence.
Rescheduling an exam or granting an exception is decided by the instructor and/or the Study Office under the study regulations; a student cannot be promised a new date automatically.
Submit a formal request through the official student administration system with supporting documents (e.g. medical certificate).
entries.contact_channel: Course instructor, then the faculty Study Office
entries.typical_response: Depends on the request; formal requests can take several working days

entries.scope: Immediate danger, injuries, hazards.
procedures: If anyone is in immediate danger call the European emergency number 112.
Move away from the hazard and keep others away.
Inform building reception / campus security so the area can be secured.
Report the hazard afterwards so it can be fixed.
entries.contact_channel: 112 in emergencies; building reception / campus security otherwise

entries.scope: University dormitory issues.
procedures: Report maintenance issues in the dormitory to the dormitory reception.
For room changes or roommate conflicts contact the dormitory office in person or via its official email channel.
entries.contact_channel: Dormitory reception / dormitory office

entries.scope: Documents and administration for international students.
procedures: Request official certificates (e.g. student status) through the student administration system or the international office.
For residence or visa matters, ask the International Student Office for guidance; they can explain which documents the authorities require.
entries.contact_channel: International Student Office

entries.scope: Library services, loans, study rooms, e-resources.
procedures: Check loan status and renew online through the library account.
Ask at the library information desk for study room bookings or e-resource access problems.
entries.contact_channel: Library information desk

entries.scope: Course registration, student status certificates, transcripts, semester enrolment, timetables.
procedures: Request official certificates (student status, transcript) through the student administration system (Neptun) using the request/form menu.
For course registration problems, check the registration period and prerequisite courses in the student administration system first.
If the system does not allow the action, contact the faculty Study Office with student ID, course code and a screenshot of the error.
Exceptions to registration deadlines are decided by the Study Office; the student should submit a formal request.
entries.contact_channel: Faculty Study Office (counter or official request form in the student administration system)
entries.typical_response: Certificates usually within a few working days; exceptions longer

entries.scope: Scholarships, tuition and fee payments, refunds, student invoices.
procedures: Check the student administration system finance menu for the status of the scholarship or payment item.
Verify that the bank account details stored in the student administration system are correct and up to date.
If a payment is missing or incorrect, contact the Student Finance Office with student ID, the payment item and the expected date.
Corrections, refunds and payment exceptions are decided by Student Finance Office staff.
entries.contact_channel: Student Finance Office (official university finance contact page)

entries.scope: Confidential psychological counselling and wellbeing support for students.
procedures: If someone is in immediate danger or thinking about harming themselves, call the European emergency number 112 now.
Book a confidential appointment with the university Student Counselling Service.
Talk to someone you trust (friend, family, mentor) and let them know how you are feeling.
For exam-related stress, the student can also ask the instructor or Study Office about available academic support.
entries.contact_channel: Student Counselling Service (official university page); 112 in emergencies
entries.typical_response: Appointments usually within days; urgent support through emergency services

entries.scope: Medical care for students, medical certificates, health insurance questions.
procedures: In a medical emergency call 112.
For non-urgent illness, visit the student/university health service or a general practitioner during opening hours.
Ask the doctor for a medical certificate if classes or exams are missed; it is needed for formal academic requests.
International students should keep their health insurance documents with them.
entries.contact_channel: University health service / general practitioner; 112 in emergencies

entries.scope: Support and reasonable adjustments for students with disabilities; physical accessibility of buildings.
procedures: Register with the university disability/accessibility support coordinator to request adjustments (e.g. extra exam time).
Report broken lifts, ramps or blocked accessible routes to building reception so they can be fixed quickly.
Adjustments for exams are approved by the coordinator and the Study Office; request them well before the exam period.
entries.contact_channel: Disability & accessibility support coordinator (official university page); building reception for physical barriers
entries.typical_response: Physical barriers: as soon as possible; adjustments: several working days

entries.scope: Harassment, discrimination, bullying and formal complaints.
procedures: If anyone is in immediate danger, call 112 or campus security.
Write down what happened (date, time, place, people involved, witnesses) and keep any messages as evidence.
Contact the student ombudsman / equal opportunities office for confidential advice on the options.
Formal complaints are investigated by authorised staff; the system cannot judge the case.
entries.contact_channel: Student ombudsman / equal opportunities office (official university page)
entries.typical_response: Initial contact within a few working days

entries.scope: University canteens, cafeterias, vending machines.
procedures: Report food quality or hygiene problems to the canteen manager on site, with date and time of purchase.
Ask canteen staff about allergen information and vegetarian/halal options before ordering.
If you feel unwell after eating, seek medical help and keep the receipt.
entries.contact_channel: Canteen manager on site

entries.scope: Lost and found items, lost student cards.
procedures: Ask at the reception / porter's desk of the building where the item was lost; found items are usually handed in there.
If the student card is lost, report it so it can be blocked and request a replacement through the student administration.
If the item was stolen, report it to campus security; for theft the police can also be contacted.
entries.contact_channel: Building reception / porter's desk

entries.scope: Student printing, scanning and copying.
procedures: Check the print credit balance on the student account and top up if needed.
Try another printer in the same building and note the printer ID of the faulty one.
Report hardware faults (paper jam, no toner) to building reception or the IT Service Desk with the printer ID.
entries.contact_channel: IT Service Desk / building reception

entries.scope: University sports facilities, sports courses and passes.
procedures: Check opening hours and booking rules of the sports facility on the official sports centre page.
Report broken or unsafe sports equipment to the staff on duty immediately and stop using it.
For sports course registration use the student administration system during the registration period.
entries.contact_channel: Sports centre reception

entries.scope: Getting to campus: public transport student passes, parking and bike storage.
procedures: Student discounts on local public transport require a valid student ID card; check the operator's official ticket rules.
For problems with local buses or trams (delays, missing service), contact the public transport operator's customer service.
For campus parking permits or bike storage ask the building reception or facilities management.
entries.contact_channel: Public transport operator customer service; building reception for parking
